attributes.residual: TWO findings the next lane needs. (1) THE JOINT-PROBE ARITHMETIC IN THE PREDECESSOR RECORD IS REFUTED, at zero build cost, by the FT record's own premise_measurement: that hypothesis proposed deleting `aRWork` (-4 B of nominal local area) and adding one s32 elsewhere (+4 B) to hold the frame at 864, but FT already measured that removing `aRWork` leaves BOTH frames at 864, and this run reproduced that (`frame: target 864 ours 864` in probe 1's slot map). There is no 4-byte hole to compensate -- `aRWork` lives in the nested `smode <= 5` block and overlays other block-scoped locals -- so that form would have measured nothing, and the 4-bytes-per-s32 figure from `one`/`zero` does not transfer to a nested block. Hence the promotion-RANKING hypothesis above. (2) F1 IS A TEMPORARY-GROUPING DIFFERENCE, not a slot rotation and not the two-slot exchange framing either. The aligned view at `fnasm game/pb/pb_frame.c pbFrameMode 0x60:0xd0 --diff` shows each mode arm runs TWO u32->f64 magic-number conversions, each needing a STAGING double and a fctiwz RESULT double, i.e. four anonymous 8-byte temporaries at 760/768/776/784. TARGET arm 1: conv1 staging 776 (`@0x68 stw r4,780(r1)`, `@0x78 stw r0,776(r1)`, `@0x8c lfd f0,776(r1)`), conv1 result 768 (`@0xa8 stfd f0,768(r1)`, `@0xb0 lwz r0,772(r1)`), conv2 staging 784, conv2 result 760. OURS: conv1 staging 768, conv1 result 760, conv2 staging 784, conv2 result 776. Both allocate conv2's staging at 784 first; the target then allocates BOTH STAGING temporaries before either result (784, 776, 768, 760) while ours allocates conv2's pair then conv1's pair. So the target groups by ROLE and we group by CONVERSION. The arbiter discipline 3 names confirms it and bounds it: `python tools/gdl/slotdiff.py game/pb/pb_frame.c pbFrameMode` at 0f4151839 prints `== pbFrameMode: target 38 slots, ours 38 -> SLOTS ALIGNED, 2 use-count deltas`, with the ONLY differing rows `USE-COUNT slot 768 target 7 vs ours 5` and `USE-COUNT slot 776 target 5 vs ours 7` and every one of the other 36 slots agreeing exactly -- so the frame is right, the slot SET is right, and the entire F1 family is the shadow of that one grouping decision. The four `stfd` insert/delete pairs are the same decision seen in time rather than in space: the target emits the second conversion's `@0xb8 stfd f0,760(r1)` AFTER the first store `@0xb4 stw r0,32(r6)`, we emit ours before it. Probe 3 proves source order cannot separate the conversions' front halves (interleaved in the target; serializing them costs 150 real), so the grouping is chosen after they are already interleaved. SEVEN source-shape probes across three lanes have now died on F1.

hypothesis.count_consequence: The intent is T958/O958 -- count PARITY, the categorical change and the whole point, since the count asymmetry is what puts this function outside every postprocessor class. Deleting `aRWork` removes exactly one `mr` (-1). If the joint edit reaches O958 with no ours-only stack slot, the axis is closed; if it reaches O958 while re-creating a +1 as a spill pair, that is the measured compensating pair in a third costume and confirms the pair rather than refuting it; if it leaves O959, the edit did not reach codegen.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- every offset, register and instruction quoted above is read from this run's own `probe --slots` and `--ops` output at 0f4151839 and from the FT record's aligned view, and is accurate. What is NOT screened is WHICH source variable the target's `r14 = r1+440` corresponds to: the mapping from `addi r14,r1,440` to `pA1 = tplA1;` is inferred from the declared stack layout comment (`u8 tplA1[88]; /* 440..527 */`) and has not been confirmed against a use site in the target's own stream, and no census of the target's promotion ORDER against our declaration order was run.
hypothesis.statement: The aRWork pair is one lever and this run measured which HALF to attack: probe 1's whole 68-real cost is that our post-edit stream promotes only FIVE pointers to callee-saved registers and spills `r1+440` to slot 756, where the target promotes SIX -- `@0x52c addi r14,r1,440` in the target against our `@0x57c lwz r3,752(r1)` at the site the target spells `@0x578 mr r3,r14`. The spilled pointer is `pA1` (line 488, `pA1 = tplA1;`, tplA1 being the 88-byte buffer at r1+440), whose live range begins LATER than the switch, so it ranks below the other five candidates. The untried joint form is therefore NOT to compensate the declaration count (this run refutes that arithmetic, see attributes.residual) but to strengthen pA1's web: delete `aRWork` so the subtraction reads `aR` directly AND hoist `pA1 = tplA1;` from line 488 to immediately after `sync0 = lbl_80343F00;` at line 370. Run the two edits JOINTLY (AGENTS discipline 6), never pA1 alone.
